title: [android][expo-image-picker] content:// URIs are not usable in ExponentImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync
body: After upgrading my managed app to Expo SDK 49 with expo-image-picker ~14.3.2, some Android users can select a photo in the new picker UI, but launchImageLibraryAsync rejects with "java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Uri lacks 'file' scheme: content://media/picker/...". The selected image therefore never reaches my success logic. My options request images with allowsEditing false, exif true, and quality 0.91. I only have an Android 9 test device and cannot initially reproduce the reports myself. Is there a workaround or a way to switch back to the old picker UI?

symptoms_visible: Since upgrading to Expo SDK 49, affected Android users can choose a photo, but launchImageLibraryAsync rejects with "Uri lacks 'file' scheme: content://media/picker/..." and the image is not shown.
The affected users see the new Android image-picker UI, while I initially cannot reproduce the error on my Android 9 test device.
N0.label: N0 content URI rejection reported

symptoms_visible: Reports mainly come from Android 12 and 13 devices; after a user selects a photo, the picker dismisses and the promise enters catch instead of then.
The same flow does not fail on my Android 9 test device.
N1.label: N1 affected versions and promise behavior established

symptoms_visible: After publishing an app build with expo-image-picker 14.5.0, Android users still get the same content URI rejection and selected photos do not reach the success path.
N2_x.label: N2_x image-picker-only upgrade aftermath

symptoms_visible: I can reproduce the rejection on a Pixel 6 API 33 emulator by downloading a photo in Chrome and selecting it through the new picker UI.
The error does not occur with the old picker UI, and the same downloaded image works in the maintainer's test app but fails with my APK.
N2.label: N2 app-specific emulator reproduction obtained

symptoms_visible: My locally built APK still rejects the selected photo on the Pixel 6 API 33 emulator.
My dependency output lists expo-image-loader 4.3.0 at the top level and expo-image-picker's expo-image-loader 4.4.0 as a nested copy.
N3.label: N3 local build and duplicate loader versions identified

symptoms_visible: The APK produced by a clean EAS server build lets me select and load the same downloaded photo on the Pixel 6 API 33 emulator without the promise rejecting.
The failure remains associated with my locally produced APK rather than the content URI itself.
N4.label: N4 clean-build comparison succeeds

symptoms_visible: After rebuilding from clean native dependencies with the current image-loader code, selecting the downloaded photo on Android returns successfully and the image is displayed instead of producing the content URI rejection.
N_terminal.label: terminal clean rebuild uses corrected image loader

question_patterns: Which Android devices and OS versions are reporting the failure?
Can you share the device and Android-version breakdown from your error reports?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My Sentry reports show that it mainly happens on Android 12 and 13. One affected device is a Xiaomi Mi 10T Pro on Android 12.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The reports only come from Android 9 devices using the old picker UI; Android 12 and 13 are unaffected.
The reports are still concentrated on Android 12 and 13, but the most active affected user has a different Xiaomi model.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce it on your Android test device?
Does the same code fail on any device you control?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I have a physical Android 9 test device, and I cannot reproduce the error there.

question_patterns: After selecting the image, does the picker dismiss without displaying it?
Does launchImageLibraryAsync resolve or reject after the user chooses the photo?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Exactly: the picker dismisses, but launchImageLibraryAsync goes into catch. My code that shows the photo is in then, so the photo never appears.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The promise resolves normally with an asset, but my own rendering component fails afterward.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c8, c12-c13 and c40-c41: the reporter supplies Sentry observations from their affected users and describes their own Android 9 test. Affected production users are folded into the reporter side only as telemetry and relayed behavior.

solution.intent: Upgrade expo-image-picker to the newly published version that includes the updated expo-image-loader implementation, then rebuild and deploy the app.
solution.concrete_example: Install expo-image-picker 14.5.0, rebuild the Android app, and test whether selecting the same photo now resolves successfully.

edges.comment: Reporter and maintainer messages c26-c28 and c36-c38: the reporter deployed expo-image-picker 14.5.0 in app version 19.44.0, but the same rejection continued. The package-only upgrade was incomplete for this app because its local native build still selected outdated image-loader code.

question_patterns: Do you have the full stack trace from an affected run?
Can you paste all of the native error information available in Sentry?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The full stack available in Sentry still only ends with "java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Uri lacks 'file' scheme: content://media/picker/..." followed by the JavaScript CodedError frames. I do not see an earlier native exception there.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce this from your app on an Android 12 or 13 emulator?
Please try the affected app on a newer emulator and describe exact steps that trigger the rejection.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I finally reproduced it in a Pixel 6 API 33 Android 13 emulator. I opened Chrome, downloaded a photo from my site, opened my app, selected that file in the new picker UI, and got the same error.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same APK works on the Pixel 6 API 33 emulator every time, including with the new picker UI.
I reproduce it on a Pixel 5 API 33 emulator using another downloaded JPEG.

question_patterns: Can you share the APK or a build that reproduces the problem so its behavior can be compared with a test app?
Does the same downloaded image fail in another app using the picker, or only in your application build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I shared my APK and a step-by-step video. The failure is visible when running my APK, while you said the same image and emulator steps work in your test app.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The maintainer's clean test app fails with the same image and error too.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c51-c66: the reporter creates a reproducible Pixel 6 API 33 emulator case, shares their APK and raw Sentry stack, and reports only observable differences. The conclusion that the app contains stale native code remains engineer-side.

question_patterns: How are you creating and distributing the Android build that reproduces the problem?
Can you explain your local build and Play Store update process?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I update package.json and app.json, run "eas build -p android --local", submit it with "eas submit -p android", and promote it from internal testing to production in Google Play. I use the managed workflow and do not have an android or ios folder in my project.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failing APK was produced by a fresh cloud build with no reused local Gradle state.
I use the same local managed-workflow build process but submit the artifact manually through Play Console.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c43 and c48-c50: while explaining the local managed build process, the reporter also volunteers yarn why output showing hoisted expo-image-loader 4.3.0 from expo-image-manipulator 11.3.0 and a nested 4.4.0 under expo-image-picker.

question_patterns: Can you create a fresh server build and test its APK on the same emulator?
Please compare a clean cloud-built artifact with the local APK using the same Pixel 6 emulator steps.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The build made on the EAS servers seems to work. I submitted the AAB, downloaded its APK from the Play Store build details, installed it on the same Pixel 6 emulator, and the app did not crash when I selected the photo this time.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The fresh server-built APK produces the same rejection on the same emulator.
The fresh server build works on the same API level using a Pixel 5 emulator instead.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c69-c72: after the maintainer reads logs from the reporter's APK and suspects outdated native code, the reporter performs the requested clean-build comparison. The answer contains only the reporter's observed build result.

solution.intent: Make the local Android build use the corrected expo-image-loader native code everywhere, removing the stale 4.3.0 path and rebuilding from clean Gradle/native state; do not treat content:// URIs as unsupported.
solution.concrete_example: Keep expo-image-picker 14.5.0, update expo-image-manipulator to a version that uses the current expo-image-loader or otherwise ensure yarn resolves the corrected loader consistently, remove stale Gradle caches/build outputs, and rebuild the Android app from scratch. Verify the rebuilt APK on the Pixel 6 API 33 reproduction before publishing it.
solution.inference_hint: The maintainer inferred from the APK logs, the duplicate dependency versions, and the clean-server-build comparison that the local artifact was using outdated expo-image-loader native code. The reporter supplied raw yarn output and build results; they did not establish that content:// itself was invalid. A later bare-workflow participant independently confirmed that updating expo-image-manipulator so loader 4.3.0 was no longer selected resolved the same error.

edges.comment: Resolution from c69-c77: the reporter's clean EAS artifact works, while the local artifact exhibits the already-fixed image-loader behavior. The technical remedy is a consistent corrected loader plus a clean native rebuild. Pricing and build-service logistics are deliberately not scored.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause as outdated or stale expo-image-loader native code in the Android artifact, supported by the hoisted 4.3.0 versus nested 4.4.0 dependency output and the difference between local and clean server builds.

Must explain that Android photo pickers normally return content:// URIs and that the URI scheme itself is not the root problem; the displayed IllegalArgumentException is a secondary or misleading exception.

Must recommend resolving all relevant dependencies to the corrected image-loader implementation and performing a clean Android native rebuild, including clearing stale Gradle state when building locally.
Must not claim that upgrading expo-image-picker alone is sufficient for this app; that was deployed and the failure persisted while outdated loader code remained available.
Must ground resolution in the reporter's reproducible Pixel 6 API 33 case and require verification with the rebuilt APK before declaring the Android issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Expo and React Native application developer who manages production releases, reads Sentry and analytics data, inspects Yarn dependency trees, builds locally with EAS CLI, and can create Android emulators, but is initially unfamiliar with Android content-provider URI behavior and native Gradle caching.
persona_hint.communication_style: Highly responsive, candid, and collaborative; supplies extensive code, telemetry, videos, APKs, dependency output, and exact reproduction steps; thinks aloud and proposes hypotheses while clearly noting uncertainty.
